hook.line: Everything in Tomás's week changes at the last minute: the meeting, the delivery, even the bank appointment. Spanish has a short, article-free phrase for that moment, and a twin for "first thing in the morning".
hook.en: They cancelled at the last minute.

examples.en: They cancelled at the last minute.

examples.es: Tengo una reunión a primera hora de la mañana.
examples.en: I have a meeting first thing in the morning.
We arrived at the last minute.
He arrived in the small hours.

examples.es: Vale cambió el menú a última hora.
examples.en: Vale changed the menu at the last minute.

rule:
Some moments of the day come as fixed phrases:

*a última hora*: at the last minute
*a primera hora*: first thing
*de madrugada*: in the small hours
*en el último minuto*: at the last minute

The *a* phrases take no article. English says "at *the* last minute"; Spanish says *a última hora*, never *a la última hora*. For "first thing in the morning", add *de la mañana*. Because *hora* is feminine, it is *última*, not *último*.
smallPrint: Teachers call these adverbial phrases of time: frozen expressions you learn whole.

options: They cancelled first thing.
They cancelled at the last minute.
They cancelled an hour ago.
We left at the last minute.
We left at midnight.
We left first thing.
He arrived in the small hours.
He arrived at the last minute.
He arrived on time.

readAndPick.es: Tengo una reunión a primera hora de la mañana.
options: I have a meeting last thing at night.
I have a meeting first thing in the morning.
I had a meeting yesterday morning.
We arrived first thing.
We arrived early.
We arrived at the last minute.

readAndPick.es: Vale cambió la receta a última hora.
options: Vale changed the recipe at the last minute.
Vale changed the recipe first thing.
Vale changed the recipe last week.
Tomorrow I'll leave at the last minute.
Yesterday I left first thing.
Tomorrow I'm leaving first thing.
He let us know first thing.
He let us know at the last moment.
He let us know right away.

yourTurn.prompt: They cancelled at the last minute. Fill the gap: Cancelaron ___ hora. (*a última* or *a la última*)
yourTurn.why: The phrase is fixed and takes no article.
*A primera hora* is the fixed phrase for first thing.

yourTurn.prompt: I have a meeting first thing in the morning.
yourTurn.answer: Tengo una reunión a primera hora de la mañana.
yourTurn.why: Add *de la mañana* after *a primera hora* to say which part of the day.

yourTurn.prompt: He arrived in the small hours.
yourTurn.why: *De madrugada* covers the hours after midnight, no article.

yourTurn.prompt: Vale changed the menu at the last minute.
yourTurn.answer: Vale cambió el menú a última hora.
accept: Vale cambió el menú en el último minuto.
Vale cambió el menú en el último momento.
yourTurn.why: *A última hora* and *en el último minuto* both mean the very last moment.

yourTurn.prompt: Say it about tomorrow: I'm leaving first thing.
yourTurn.why: The phrase stays the same; only the verb moves to the present.

yourTurn.prompt: They always cancel at the last minute.
yourTurn.why: The phrase works with any verb and any time.

pitfalls.why: Almost. English likes "the", but this Spanish phrase has no article.
*Hora* is feminine, so the word before it is *última*.

personal: Tell us about something that changed at the last minute. Start with *… a última hora.*
